items.title: [https://nvbugs/6732110][fix] Cache the split communicator in a new `MNNVLAllReduce.allreduce_mnnvl_pending_c…
items.body:
## Summary
- **Root cause**: The MNNVL workspace is published only after fabric allocation succeeds, so a failed `McastGPUBuffer` construction leaves the cache empty and every later `AllReduce` module issues another world-wide `mpi_comm().Split()`, leaking one communicator per layer until MPI communicator resources are exhausted and ranks die asymmetrically.
- **Fix**: Cache the split communicator in a new `MNNVLAllReduce.allreduce_mnnvl_pending_comms` ClassVar, reuse it on retry, and hand ownership to the workspace at publish time so the checkpoint hooks stay byte-identical to upstream; construction retries are preserved (9→9).
- **Original test**: `python .repair-bot/repro.py`
- Automated fix generated by repair-bot

## Test plan
- [x] Verify fix on the same GPU type as the original failure
- [x] Check for regressions in related tests

## Links
- Bug: https://nvbugs/6732110


## Reproduction comparison
- Failed commit: repro_on_failed_commit at c21a90820a5ac0c2657c37073ff773c561dde75e
  Signature: CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN, as on the GB300 run).
- ToT: repro_on_tot at b349408280d44363fbe1e57c593a4d63ce63d87c
  Signature: CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN, as on the GB300 run).
- Signature relation: needs_agent

`MNNVLAllReduce` now caches split communicators for unpublished workspaces. Failed workspace construction can reuse the cached communicator and avoid MPI communicator leaks. Successful construction transfers communicator ownership to the published workspace. Review should verify cache cleanup, mapping-key stability, and retry behavior under concurrent construction.

## QA Engineer Review

No test changes.

items.title: [None][feat] Add lightweight per-pool KV cache utilization logging
items.body:
## Description

The aggregate `kv_cache_util` iteration log can hide a nearly full KV pool. Add `TLLM_KV_POOL_LOG_INTERVAL=N` to inspect GPU and host pools without enabling iteration performance statistics.

With `print_iter_log: true`, V2 uses a lightweight CPU-side GPU capacity snapshot on every logged iteration, including when the interval is disabled. Sampled iterations reuse that snapshot for GPU pool values and read host counters once. The interval defaults to `0` (disabled); use `50` for periodic samples or `1` for every iteration. Existing rank filtering applies. Warmup skips pool samples, repeated iteration numbers are sampled only once, and unsampled lines omit pool fields. Legacy managers retain their existing aggregate log.

The interval is validated at construction; empty means disabled. A warning explains when the setting cannot take effect. The cache manager logs the cold pool mapping at construction alongside the existing GPU mapping because GPU and host pool IDs are independent. Disk capacity is excluded; missing host tiers and zero-capacity pools report `N/A`.

- GPU utilization: `1 - (free + evictable) / total`, aggregated by slot count.
- Host occupancy: `1 - free / total`, including evictable cached pages.

```text
kv_cache_util = 0.600, kv_cache_gpu_pool_util = [0:0.900;1:0.500], kv_cache_host_pool_util = [0:0.750],
```

The diagnostic does not collect/reset iteration deltas or add CUDA synchronization or cross-rank communication. Sampling can miss transient peaks; formatting and log output still have a cost. No measured performance improvement is claimed.

## Test Coverage

- Added 23 CPU test cases covering GPU/host capacity semantics, independent groups, disk exclusion, missing/zero capacity, construction mapping, snapshot reuse, sampling deduplication, warmup, disabled/V1 behavior, interval validation, and log/rank filtering.
- All 23 passed in an isolated Python 3.12 harness on macOS with native/GPU imports stubbed. The harness loads the production profiling module and extracts the production KV methods; it validates Python control flow and counter reads, not native integration or the normal TensorRT-LLM pytest environment.
- Python compilation and `git diff --check` passed. The final documentation/comment correction preserves executable Python behavior; applicable pre-commit and DCO hooks passed.
- Pending: run `pytest tests/unittest/_torch/executor/test_kv_cache_utilization_log.py` in the TensorRT-LLM environment, a GPU inference smoke test, and an overhead A/B with identical workload/log/rank settings and interval `0` versus `50`.

## PR Checklist

- [x] Reviewed the applicable checklist: scoped change, documentation and regression coverage included, no new dependencies, no LLM argument/schema changes, and no ownership or architecture changes.

items.title: [None][feat] Support attention DP in KV cache connectors
items.body:
## Description

The generic KV connector previously assumed that every rank handled the same requests: rank 0 made scheduler decisions, and transfer completion waited for all workers. ADP owners can process different requests and issue different numbers of allocation callbacks, so those connector collectives cannot be used for ADP.

This change creates a connector scheduler adapter and worker on every ADP rank. Lookup, allocation feedback, transfer metadata and completion follow the local request owner. All adapters can connect to one shared logical storage pool and reuse compatible KV content produced by other owners. For example, an owner handling three requests can complete its transfers without requiring connector callbacks from an idle peer. The existing TP path retains rank-0 scheduling and completion across all attention shards.

### Changes

- Require both scheduler and worker classes to declare `supports_attention_dp = True`; instantiate adapters on every ADP rank. Existing third-party connectors remain gated until they implement this contract.
- Add `SchedulerOutput.attention_dp_rank` to identify the owner of local block IDs. Keep reusable content keys independent of the ADP rank.
- Remove cross-owner connector broadcasts and completion collectives under ADP. Request and transfer state remain local to each adapter.
- Exclude compute dummy requests from connector lookup, allocation feedback, metadata and request-finished callbacks. If asynchronous loading empties an owner's batch, attempt late dummy padding while preserving the real transfer plan.
- Defer cancellation of tracked asynchronous transfers until worker completion, and retire per-request connector metadata after the finish callback.
- Update the persistent-cache example to share a filesystem directory across owners, use stable SHA-256 keys over the complete prefix and cache salt, and atomically publish completed files.
- Add ownership, idle-owner, completion, cancellation and shared-pool regressions, plus a two-GPU serving regression covering balanced and unequal-length batches with overlap enabled and disabled.

### Scope

Initial support uses the V1 cache manager, one primary GPU pool, one attention worker per ADP owner, PP=1, CP=1, beam width 1 and guaranteed-no-evict scheduling. Existing exclusions for VSWA, internal host offload and Mamba/hybrid state remain. V2, heterogeneous attention shards and elastic peer-HBM allocation require separate integration.

items.title: [#17436][perf] Cache request logit bias on device during sampling
items.body:
## Description

Fixes #17436.

OpenAI `logit_bias` creates a separate dense CPU vocabulary tensor for each request. The sampler deduplicates by tensor identity, then stacks and uploads those tensors again at every decode iteration. With 110 requests and a 248,320-token vocabulary, this repeats a 109.26 MB bias transfer per iteration even though each request's bias is immutable.

Cache the device bias on the request after its first use. A Triton kernel reads a per-row address table and adds the cached biases directly to FP32 logits in place. This removes the steady-state CPU stack, repeated full-vocabulary H2D transfer, and gathered GPU bias temporary. A padded batch of 128 rows transfers a 1 KiB address table each step. Initial per-request bias uploads still occur.

- Support contiguous FP32 CPU biases and contiguous FP32 CUDA logits for single-step, single-beam requests, including CUDA Graph batch padding and mixed biased/unbiased requests.
- Preserve the existing implementation for other dtypes/layouts, multi-step or multi-beam batches, and host preparation during graph capture. This change adds no public API or configuration option.
- Retain device tensors as explicit custom-op inputs, record their sampling-stream use, and wait for an upload event when the consumer stream changes.
- Clear request-owned caches during resource release and executor shutdown. The cache costs one FP32 vocabulary tensor per active biased request, approximately 0.95 MiB at this vocabulary size; it does not deduplicate equal biases across requests.

The current-main port uses `LlmRequest.py_embedding_bias`, `sampler_features.apply_embedding_bias`, and the centralized `_free_request_resources` path.

## Performance

**Benchmark scope:** the following end-to-end measurements validate the implementation on TensorRT-LLM **v1.3.0rc22**, commit `8ba93401976877ca2a390104829dd0d54cf2f30f`, with PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130. This PR ports that implementation to current `main`; full current-main serving validation remains pending.

| Model and deployment | Bias | Before output tokens/s | After output tokens/s | Change |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B, BF16 weights, 1 × H800/SM90, TP1 | On | 3,318.18 | 6,573.03 | **+98.09%** |
| Same 0.8B deployment | Off | 7,126.05 | 7,137.12 | +0.16% |
| Local Qwen3.5-397B-A17B FP8 checkpoint, 8 × H800/SM90, TP8/EP8 | On | 959.45 | 1,073.64 | **+11.90%** |
| Same 397B deployment | Off | 1,088.81 | 1,089.73 | +0.085% |

- Shared workload: closed-loop concurrency 110, 220 requests per phase, 11,970 actual input tokens and 640 output tokens per request, 1,206 bias entries at -100, `temperature=0`, `top_p=1`, `ignore_eos=true`, thinking disabled, non-streaming chat completions. All formal requests succeeded with the specified token counts.
- Both deployments use FP8 KV cache, chunked prefill, CUDA Graph padding, disabled KV block reuse, and four postprocessing workers. `OMP_NUM_THREADS=MKL_NUM_THREADS=1`. Throughput includes prefill, decode, scheduling, and HTTP overhead; it is the whole instance's output throughput. All timed server processes were warmed up and never enabled Torch/Nsight profiling.
- 0.8B: max batch 384, max tokens per iteration 32,768, max sequence length 65,536, KV free-memory fraction 0.75. P50 request latency: **20.95 → 10.35 s**. An independent warmed patched process measured 6,629.72 tokens/s, within 0.86% of the table's patched result.
- 397B: max batch 128, max tokens per iteration 8,192, max sequence length 16,384, KV free-memory fraction 0.80, attention DP disabled, CUTLASS MoE. The local FP8 checkpoint uses dynamic activation quantization and 128×128 weight blocks. Both versions set `TRTLLM_FLA_DISABLE_FLASHINFER_GDN=1` because the default FlashInfer GDN decode path hit a TP8 alignment error in this environment.
- 397B runs `on → off → on` per version, after an additional 110-request/128-output-token warmup. Biased runs were 951.51/967.52 tokens/s before and 1,070.60/1,076.69 after; the table pools each pair as total tokens / total time. P50 over the 440 biased requests: **71.24 → 63.88 s**. The bias throughput penalty versus each version's no-bias control decreased from **11.88% to 1.48%**. All 1,320 formal requests passed.

An **independent 0.8B profile**, separate from the throughput runs, covered 20 steady-state decode iterations:

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median interval between CUDA graph launches | 30.45 ms | 13.77 ms |
| CPU `aten::cat` calls | 20 | 0 |
| 109.26 MB bias H2D copies | 20 | 0 |
| Total H2D bytes per iteration, including unrelated metadata | 110.046 MB | 0.786 MB |
| New fused bias kernel, mean duration | — | 108.14 µs |

The 397B measurements use a local converted FP8 checkpoint. These results characterize the specified workloads and configurations; they are not a hardware throughput tuning sweep.

## Test Coverage

Added `tests/unittest/_torch/sampler/test_embedding_bias_cache.py` with 88 cases covering numerical equivalence, vocabulary tile boundaries, heterogeneous and mixed biases, the 110-request/128-row padding case, cache reuse/replacement, fallback behavior, input snapshots, cross-stream use, early release, CUDA Graph replay, request churn, and resource cleanup.

Validation on the benchmark implementation:

- **88/88 GPU tests passed**, including a fresh rerun while preparing this PR.
- **88/88 tests passed under Compute Sanitizer memcheck; zero device memory errors.** Used `--show-backtrace no --report-api-errors no` because this environment probes optional CUDA APIs and backtrace retention interferes with the Python object-lifetime assertions. Device memory checking and the assertions remained enabled.
- **16 HTTP semantic checks passed**: different requests with positive/negative token biases generated their intended forced tokens. These checks completed before the timed serving runs.
- The two model benchmarks and independent 0.8B profile above passed.

Current-main port: **88/88 cases passed in an isolated GPU compatibility harness** for the ported cache, application, and resource-release logic using the available rc22 binary environment. The helper was AST-checked against the measured implementation with only the request-field rename; the unchanged registered device op was reused, and the current-main application/resource-release functions were executed from source. This does not load the complete current-main executor or replace full current-main integration/CI validation. The PR remains a draft pending that validation. The repository's lightweight mypy check passed for its 17 configured source files.

## PR Checklist

- The change addresses one sampling performance issue and preserves unsupported-path behavior.
- No public API/configuration change, new dependency, or ownership change.
- New code paths have GPU numerical and lifecycle tests; scope and benchmark provenance are documented above.
- [x] Repository pre-commit checks passed, including lint/formatting, vendor/test-list validation, lightweight mypy, and the commit-message DCO check. The commit was created with `git commit -s`.
- [ ] Current-main integration/CI validation completed; ready for review.

items.title: [https://nvbugs/6739553][fix] Isolate the FlashInfer cubin cache per rank
items.body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

- Removes default `FLASHINFER_CUBIN_DIR` assignments from `mpi_session.py` and `trtllm-llmapi-launch`.
- FlashInfer now derives downloaded-artifact storage from the per-rank `FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE`, preventing concurrent header replacement during JIT compilation.
- Explicit `FLASHINFER_CUBIN_DIR` values and installed read-only cubin packages remain supported.
- Documentation explains cache isolation and explicit override behavior.
- The scope is limited to FlashInfer cache handling. The main regression risk is incorrect behavior when users provide explicit or shared cubin directories.

## QA Engineer Review

- Updates `tests/unittest/llmapi/_run_mpi_comm_task.py` and `tests/unittest/llmapi/test_flashinfer_workspace.py`.
- Tests now verify that `FLASHINFER_CUBIN_DIR` remains unset by default and that explicit values propagate correctly.
- Removes the waiver for `TestDeepSeekV32::test_nvfp4_multi_gpus_piecewise_cuda_graph[mtp3_fp8kv_chunked]`.
- Coverage is **sufficient** for the changed environment behavior and the previously waived integration test. Verify that the modified unit tests are present in the appropriate CI or manual-QA lists.

## Per-File QA Perspective

- `docs/source/llm-api/index.md`: Documents per-rank FlashInfer artifact caching and explicit `FLASHINFER_CUBIN_DIR` behavior.
- `tensorrt_llm/llmapi/mpi_session.py`: Changes the default environment behavior by leaving `FLASHINFER_CUBIN_DIR` unset. Verify isolated workspace derivation and explicit override propagation.
- `tensorrt_llm/llmapi/trtllm-llmapi-launch`: Removes automatic shared cubin-directory setup. Verify persistent and temporary workspace handling and multi-rank JIT compilation.
- `tests/integration/test_lists/waives.txt`: Removes the DeepSeek V32 NVFP4 multi-GPU waiver. Verify that the test runs in the intended integration-test configuration.
- `tests/unittest/llmapi/_run_mpi_comm_task.py`: Verifies that worker bootstrap leaves `FLASHINFER_CUBIN_DIR` unset. Confirm the test is included in the applicable CI test list.
- `tests/unittest/llmapi/test_flashinfer_workspace.py`: Covers workspace isolation for unset and explicitly configured cubin directories. Confirm the test is included in the applicable CI test list.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

`TestDeepSeekV32::test_nvfp4_multi_gpus_piecewise_cuda_graph[mtp3_fp8kv_chunked]`
fails intermittently on the 8-GPU B200 post-merge stage (5 hits in the last 30
days, e.g. `LLM/main/L0_PostMerge #2955`, stage `DGX_B200-8_GPUs-PyTorch-1`).
The failure is a FlashInfer JIT compile error, not an accuracy or hang problem:

```
error: ... has already been defined
```

for the `fused_moe_trtllm_sm100` translation unit, with the *same*
`SfLayoutDecl.h` shown as `Fetching` four times in the log.

### Why it happens

Two conditions have to hold together:

1. **One header is reachable through two distinct `-I` paths.** FlashInfer's
   `moe_utils.py:59-66` symlinks the trtllm-gen export directory at a different
   level than `fused_moe.py:286-290` does, and `fused_moe.py:351-352` puts both
   roots on the include path. nvcc/EDG caches `#pragma once` per path; for a
   second path it compares `(mtime, size)`, so a changed mtime makes it treat
   one header as two files. On its own this is harmless — both paths resolve to
   identical bytes.

2. **The same header is replaced underneath a translation unit while it
   compiles.** `FLASHINFER_CUBIN_DIR` does not only hold runtime cubins: it also
   holds 17 trtllm-gen export headers, which are *compiler inputs* and are the
   targets of the two symlinks above. `cubin_loader.py:206-233` verifies a
   download's checksum *before* taking the download lock, so several ranks can
   fetch the same header concurrently and each finish with an atomic rename —
   and an atomic rename always changes the inode and the mtime.

Condition 2 only exists because both launch paths forced `FLASHINFER_CUBIN_DIR`
back to a single shared `$HOME/.cache/flashinfer/cubins`, even though #18278 had
already given every rank its own `FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE`. So the workspace
was isolated while the directory that actually feeds nvcc stayed shared.

Each condition alone is insufficient — that was confirmed by controlled
experiments (dual `-I` with a stable directory does not reproduce; a shared
directory with a single `-I` root does not reproduce). Together they reproduce.

### The fix

Remove the two overrides
(`tensorrt_llm/llmapi/trtllm-llmapi-launch`, `tensorrt_llm/llmapi/mpi_session.py`)
so the cubin cache follows the isolated workspace instead. With the variable
unset and no `flashinfer-cubin` package installed, `flashinfer/jit/env.py:107`
derives the directory from `FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE`, which is already
per-rank. No new environment variable is introduced; an explicit
`FLASHINFER_CUBIN_DIR` still wins (escape hatch), and an installed
`flashinfer-cubin` package stays shared because it is read-only.

Condition 1 remains an upstream FlashInfer inconsistency and is latent without
condition 2; it is not addressed here.

## Test Coverage

**Updated unit tests** (they asserted the removed behaviour):

- `tests/unittest/llmapi/test_flashinfer_workspace.py` — now asserts
  `FLASHINFER_CUBIN_DIR` is *not* set by the launcher and that an explicit value
  is still honoured.
- `tests/unittest/llmapi/_run_mpi_comm_task.py` — same expectation on the pool
  bootstrap path.

**8-rank A/B against the unmodified parent commit**, run on both paths that used
to set the variable. Every rank produced a probe record in both arms, so neither
arm is vacuous:

```
                                 ranks setting        distinct
                                 FLASHINFER_CUBIN_DIR directories
launcher (trtllm-llmapi-launch)
  before                              8/8                 1
  after                               0/8                 0
pool bootstrap (mpi_session.py)
  before                              8/8                 1
  after                               0/8                 0
```

`FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE` stays distinct across all 8 ranks in both arms, so
the isolation added by #18278 is preserved. With the variable unset,
flashinfer-python 0.6.18 (pinned in `requirements.txt:67`) resolves per-rank
directories such as `rank-N/.cache/flashinfer/cubins`, which removes condition 2
outright.

**Reproduction of the original failure** on 8xB200 required a cold JIT cache
plus both conditions armed; the resulting log matches the CI signature (same
header fetched four times, then `has already been defined`).

**Un-waive.** #18889 waived
`accuracy/test_llm_api_pytorch.py::TestDeepSeekV32::test_nvfp4_multi_gpus_piecewise_cuda_graph[mtp3_fp8kv_chunked]`
in `tests/integration/test_lists/waives.txt` so that post-merge 2955 could go
green. This PR removes that single line (the unrelated entry the same PR added
for nvbugs/6693990 is left alone), so the test runs again. It lives in the
8-GPU B200 `pre_merge` block of `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_dgx_b200.yml`,
so this PR's own CI exercises the failure's native environment end to end.

- PR Follows [TRT-LLM CODING GUIDELINES](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/CODING_GUIDELINES.md) to the best of your knowledge.

items.title: [None][fix] Fix KV cache size estimation with Qwen3.5 + EAGLE3
items.body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

- The draft KV-cache cost path now resolves the manager class from the effective draft configuration.
- One-model draft costing no longer reuses the target model’s KV cache manager.
- This fixes the `ValueError` risk for Qwen3.5 linear attention with an EAGLE3 llama-style drafter.
- The change aligns EAGLE3 behavior with the external drafter path.
- No public API or unrelated behavior changes are introduced.

## QA Engineer Review

- `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_kv_cache_budget_split.py` was updated.
- The test setup now includes `sparse_attention_config`, `_max_beam_width`, and `_kv_connector_manager`.
- The manager-class assertion now covers all parameterized speculative modes, including MTP Eagle.
- The tests cover manager selection and KV-cache budget calculation for one-model and external-drafter paths.
- Coverage verdict: sufficient.

## Per-File QA Perspective

- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/_util.py`: QA should verify KV-cache budget estimation for Qwen3.5 linear attention with EAGLE3 and external drafters. The draft configuration must select its own KV cache manager without changing target-model behavior.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_kv_cache_budget_split.py`: The test covers draft manager selection and KV-cache budget calculation across speculative modes, including MTP Eagle. This is a unit test and does not require an integration test-list entry.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

This PR fixes the bug reported in issue #18449. In particular, TRT-LLM crashes during the KV cache size estimation phase when using a Qwen3.5 model (i.e., linear attention) combined with an EAGLE3 drafter (llama-style); this happens because, during size estimation, the draft model shares the base model's KV cache manager class, leading to a `ValueError` and a crash.

This PR applies the fix suggested in the issue itself, having the EAGLE3 branch also request a specific class for the KV cache manager like in the external drafter case.

## Test Coverage

Tests have been updated to ensure that the EAGLE3 path also requests its own KV cache manager class.

items.title: [None][feat] GVR prescore tier for the DeepSeek-V4 indexer decode path (FP4 cache, opt-in)
items.body:
## Summary

Adds a prescore tier to the emission-assisted GVR Top-K decode path: the previous step's Top-K (plus both neighbours and the newest 4096 positions) is re-scored on the current query by one CuTe DSL kernel, and the sample's k-th score becomes a *sound* lower bound of the true k-th; the FP4 indexer scorer then emits every position at or above that line into a single candidate segment and the Top-K consumer admits the list on the emitter's exact count. This removes the closed-loop line extrapolation (three lines, three-segment exact-claim emission, per-layer tensor-op fitting) and its fallbacks: on real SWE-bench text the list is admitted on every row (0 fallbacks over 36k layer-steps in captures; 4/4 chained engine-glue tests value-exact). End to end on DeepSeek-V4-Flash (8xB200, TP8/EP8, real SWE-bench prompts, 64k-1M, batch 1-8) the prescore tier runs at parity with the stock path (0.99-1.04x decode step) where the closed-loop tier costs 1.22-1.30x; it is opt-in and stays off by default.

## What changes

- **Sound lines instead of extrapolated ones.** `gvr_prescore_fp4.py` (block-scaled tcgen05 MMA, ping-pong compute groups, 4096-bin mirrored-magnitude histogram, PDL) writes t0 = bin lower edge of the sample k-th minus a relative slack into the packed seed row; the sample is a sub-multiset of the row, so n(>= t0) >= K always holds. Rows without K distinct finite samples get non-finite lines and take the stock path.
- **Single-band emission.** The FP4 scorer's emission mixin gains `cand_single_band`: every hit at or above t0 goes to segment C through the claim window; no per-band exact-claim atomics, n1/n2 stay exact from the seed counters.
- **Exact-count admission and filtered walk in the consumer.** `gvr_topk_decode.py` admits single-band rows on the emitter's exact count (packed row col 3), maps every ordinal into segment C, and cuts at the tightest of {t2, t1, t0} whose exact count fits [K, B*] with the value-filtered walk; over-capacity rows (n0 > kC) fall back to the stock path exactly.
- **Fused prescore.** The prescore kernel ends at its histogram atomics (no tile counter, no last-CTA finalize); the FP4 scorer derives the three lines from the row histogram at its q-transition (128-thread scan per math warpgroup, same arithmetic as the finalize) and the row's first CTA publishes them into the seed row; the top-k resets the histogram after its PDL wait and the prescore's tile-0 CTA resets the scorer's accumulation slots. This is the prescore kernel's only mode.
- **Prior mirrored by the kernel.** An `emit_prev` epilogue writes the final indices and per-entry neighbour-duplicate flags into the caller-owned prior, so the next step's prescore needs no host copy or bitmap kernel.
- **Glue on the fused emission base.** `GvrEmissionState` gains the prescore scratch (cross-layer shared, growth-only, capture-safe), `prescore_lines`, and single-band kwargs; `TopK.prepare_gvr_emission(prescore=...)` plans the tier per step; routing opens the list tier from 32768 compressed positions and caps single-band batches at 64.
- **Compatibility.** The three-band closed-loop path is unchanged when the prescore is off; MTP (next_n > 1) rows and FP8 (DeepSeek-V3.2) caches keep the closed-loop tier; the FP8 scorer, the stock engines and the self-sampling engine are untouched.

## Enablement and dispatch

| Path | Selection (`sparse_attention_config`) |
|---|---|
| Hint-free self-sampling GVR Top-K | `enable_heuristic_topk: true` (default engine, `use_self_sampling_topk: true`) |
| Temporal-hint GVR Top-K | `enable_heuristic_topk: true`, `use_self_sampling_topk: false` |
| Closed-loop emission (3-band list / counts / rungs) | temporal-hint engine + `use_gvr_emission: true`, FP4 indexer cache |
| Prescore tier (this PR) | closed-loop prerequisites + `use_gvr_prescore: true` (new field, default off), `next_n == 1`, compressed length >= 32768, batch <= 64 |

`use_gvr_prescore` threads through `DSAParams` / `DSAMetadataParams` like `use_gvr_emission`; unmet prerequisites keep the closed-loop tier (emission on) or the stock path; a prescore row whose list overflows kC or whose sample has fewer than K finite scores takes the stock path in-kernel (exact).

## Validation

### At a glance

| Area | Result |
|---|---|
| Operator correctness | gvr 362 passed + 1 xpassed, tiers 95 passed / 8 skipped, fp4 emission subset 280 passed, fp8 176 passed (file identical to main), dsa `gvr_prescore or use_gvr` 11 passed (pytest -n 8, B200, this branch on main 140e1a208a with a wheel built from it) |
| Engine glue | chained FP4 test, cr 1/4 x batch 2/8/16, 4 steps: 4/4 value-exact vs the FP4 logits reference; exact count >= K and no overflow on every row |
| End-to-end exactness | 256k B=1 and 1M B=1 (deterministic baseline cells): 136/136 output tokens identical across stock / closed-loop / prescore |
| End-to-end decode step (before the kernel changes in this PR) | prescore 0.99-1.04x of stock across 9 cells (64k-1M, B 1/4/8, OSL 136) and 1.05x at OSL 1024 (64k, 256k; 4 pairs); closed-loop 1.22-1.30x |
| Kernel-level chain span per layer | prescore 1.47x / 1.06x of stock V1 and 1.63x / 1.63x of V2 at 64k / 256k (B=1) after the count-publication fix (19.4 / 22.5 us); the FP4 scorer's emission overhead is 0.8 us at 64k (was 2.4) and 1.6 us at 256k (was 5.9) |
| Accuracy | GSM8K strict-match 1319 samples: stock 95.45 +-0.57, closed-loop 95.53 +-0.57, prescore 95.00 +-0.60 (within one standard error) |

### End-to-end decode step

**Setup:** 8xB200, TP8/EP8, DeepSeek-V4-Flash (FP4 indexer cache, K=512), real SWE-bench prompts (20 instances concatenated, rotated per request, cut to ISL), OSL 136 with the 8-token generation subtracted, 2 pairs per cell, CUDA graphs on, chunked prefill 8192, KV fraction 0.7. `off` = stock, `cl` = closed-loop emission, `ps` = this PR. Ratios are candidate / stock (below 1.0 = faster).

| ISL | B | off ms | cl ms | ps ms | cl/off | ps/off |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64k | 1 | 6.30 | 7.83 | 6.35 | 1.242 | 1.007 |
| 64k | 4 | 6.95 | 8.61 | 7.12 | 1.239 | 1.025 |
| 64k | 8 | 7.27 | 9.44 | 7.51 | 1.299 | 1.034 |
| 128k | 1 | 6.36 | 7.98 | 6.45 | 1.256 | 1.014 |
| 128k | 4 | 7.05 | 8.78 | 7.24 | 1.245 | 1.027 |
| 128k | 8 | 7.43 | 9.67 | 7.70 | 1.301 | 1.036 |
| 256k | 1 | 6.45 | 8.15 | 6.66 | 1.265 | 1.033 |
| 256k | 4 | 7.24 | 9.07 | 7.48 | 1.253 | 1.033 |
| 1M | 1 | 6.98 | 8.55 | 6.94 | 1.225 | 0.994 |

The 1M cells run all three arms with `TRTLLM_GVR_TIERS_DISABLE=1` (the stock tiered reg kernel does not compile at npad = 262144 under cutlass-dsl 4.5.0).

**OSL 1024, 4 pairs (per-pair spread <= 0.03%), B=1, engines whose static length reaches the list tier:**

| ISL (engine max_seq_len) | off ms | ps ms | ps/off |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64k (133,120) | 5.96 | 6.25 | 1.050 |
| 256k (266,240) | 6.41 | 6.72 | 1.048 |

Routing note: with a 69,632-token engine the same 64k prompt sits below the list floor (17,408 compressed positions) and the emission path used to fall to the closed-loop rungs tier (8.20 ms vs 5.98 ms stock); this PR routes such steps to the stock path when the prescore is enabled (list tier or nothing).

### Operator performance

**Kernel-level chain (nsys, device 0, DeepSeek-V4-Flash tp8 B200, real SWE-bench prompts, 80 decode iterations; per indexer layer, us).** `sum` adds the chain kernels' durations; `span` is first-kernel start to top-k end and credits PDL overlap. Stock V1 = the tiered CuTe GVR (in-tree kernel at 1M via `TRTLLM_GVR_TIERS_DISABLE=1`), V2 = hint-free self-sampling (`TRTLLM_GVR_SELF_SAMPLING=1`). Measured before the rebase onto main 140e1a208a; the kernel sources (`gvr_topk_decode.py`, `gvr_prescore_fp4*.py`, `fp4_paged_mqa_logits.py`, `gvr_emission.py`, `gvr_routing.py`) are byte-identical on this branch.

| Cell | Stock V1 span | V2 span | Closed-loop span | Prescore span (v0 -> pad-free -> fused -> count publication fix, this PR) | Prescore sum (pad-free -> fused -> fix) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64k B=1 | 13.2 | 11.9 | 20.8 | 24.8 -> 20.7 -> 20.0 -> 19.4 | 25.8 -> 22.6 -> 20.4 |
| 256k B=1 | 21.2 | 13.8 | ~32 | 34.1 -> 27.2 -> 26.8 -> 22.5 | 33.8 -> 32.5 -> 23.5 |
| 1M B=1 | 35.4 | 17.8 | ~34 | 33.6 -> 29.2 -> 29.0 -> (not re-measured) | 36.0 -> 33.7 |
| 64k B=8 (sum, 8 rows per layer) | 13.6 | 12.6 | - | - | 24.2 -> 22.2 |

Per-kernel (this PR, us): fused prescore 4.6 / 4.9 / 4.7 (was 7.6 / 7.7 / 7.4 with the tile counter and last-CTA finalize; latency-bound, flat in row length); FP4 scorer 5.6 / 7.0 at 64k / 256k vs stock 4.8 / 5.4 (was 7.2 / 11.3 before the count-publication fix: the row-end seed counts were published with one same-address red.global.add per warp per counter, ~7,000 per row per layer, which serialize in the L2 atomic unit and hold the kernel's completion; they are now summed per warpgroup in SMEM and published once per counter per warpgroup; skipping the publication entirely measures 4.9 / 5.9, so the remaining gap is the drain of the last reductions, and the per-tile emission work itself is 0.2 us); list consumer 9.7 / 11.0 vs stock top-k 7.9 / 15.3 (V1) and 6.7 / 7.7 (V2), the consumer gaining because its PDL wait covered the scorer's reduction drain. Pad-free emission cut the consumer 12.7 -> 11.3, 21.0 -> 14.5, 17.0 -> 14.2. The fused prescore shortens the prescore grid by 2.8 us (length independent) but not the chain span: the scorer is PDL-launched at the prescore's trigger (~4.2 us after its start) and its own duration (7.5 / 12.2 / 15.1 us) already covered the removed tail; its CTAs cannot co-reside with prescore CTAs (register file), so the chain stays bound by prescore tiles + scorer + top-k tail.

Prescore kernel in isolation (B200): 5.1 us at B=8, 8.0 us at B=64, 12.2 us at B=64 with the 4096 window (K=1024).

**Cold-L2 operator comparison vs the default self-sampling top-k (V2), batch-replicated protocol.** Per cell: one real row (loncheng's random-prompt decode capture, `decode.k_cache` pages + q + weights; q scales neutral because the capture lacks them, identical for both arms) replicated in all B slots; 192 MB L2 flush before every launch; no PDL on either arm; arm A = scorer + V2 top-k, arm B = prescore + emitting scorer + list consumer, each timed as one unit; launches cycle over every distinct (layer, step) row of the bucket (189-420); cell = geometric mean of per-launch t_A / t_B (>1 = this PR faster); prev top-k for arm B = the chain's own previous-step output. All launches of both arms value-exact. The tier is forced on in every cell (production routes it from 128k, B <= 64).

Pro (K=1024):

| ISL \ B | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 | 128 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4k | 0.61 | 0.63 | 0.61 | 0.62 | 0.60 | 0.54 | 0.51 | 0.43 |
| 8k | 0.58 | 0.56 | 0.56 | 0.55 | 0.56 | 0.49 | 0.47 | 0.40 |
| 16k | 0.56 | 0.55 | 0.56 | 0.57 | 0.55 | 0.48 | 0.46 | 0.40 |
| 32k | 0.61 | 0.57 | 0.57 | 0.55 | 0.53 | 0.50 | 0.47 | 0.41 |
| 64k | 0.63 | 0.62 | 0.57 | 0.62 | 0.56 | 0.53 | 0.51 | 0.49 |
| 128k | 0.60 | 0.63 | 0.61 | 0.61 | 0.60 | 0.58 | 0.56 | 0.51 |
| 256k | 0.67 | 0.65 | 0.65 | 0.64 | 0.68 | 0.59 | 0.57 | 0.55 |
| 512k | 0.71 | 0.70 | 0.71 | 0.69 | 0.67 | 0.60 | 0.63 | 0.60 |
| 1M | 0.60 | 0.60 | 0.61 | 0.61 | 0.61 | 0.60 | 0.68 | 0.62 |

Flash (K=512):

| ISL \ B | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 | 128 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4k | 0.59 | 0.62 | 0.59 | 0.61 | 0.58 | 0.54 | 0.51 | 0.42 |
| 8k | 0.70 | 0.71 | 0.70 | 0.69 | 0.65 | 0.58 | 0.54 | 0.45 |
| 16k | 0.60 | 0.60 | 0.61 | 0.60 | 0.58 | 0.52 | 0.48 | 0.41 |
| 32k | 0.61 | 0.62 | 0.59 | 0.57 | 0.55 | 0.53 | 0.48 | 0.43 |
| 64k | 0.67 | 0.67 | 0.60 | 0.64 | 0.60 | 0.59 | 0.55 | 0.52 |
| 128k | 0.63 | 0.63 | 0.65 | 0.65 | 0.65 | 0.64 | 0.59 | 0.55 |
| 256k | 0.73 | 0.72 | 0.73 | 0.70 | 0.88 | 0.66 | 0.67 | 0.62 |
| 512k | 1.24 | 1.18 | 1.18 | 1.10 | 1.01 | 1.06 | 0.74 | 0.65 |
| 1M | 1.58 | 1.52 | 1.44 | 1.28 | 1.11 | 1.13 | 0.83 | 0.70 |

Mean us (V2 | PR) at the anchors: Pro 64k B=1 16.4 | 26.0, Pro 1M B=1 26.3 | 44.5; Flash 64k B=1 16.4 | 24.6, Flash 1M B=1 80.0 | 38.0, Flash 1M B=128 397 | 567. With the engine's recorded previous top-k as the prior (loose under the neutral-scale scoring) every Pro cell is 0.39-0.64 and Flash 512k/1M stays >= 1.0 only at B <= 8. The prescore chain therefore beats V2 only on Flash rows of 512k-1M at B <= 32; everywhere else V2 is faster, which is why the tier stays off by default.

### Accuracy

**GSM8K strict match, 5-shot, TP=EP=8, MTP0, 1319 samples, one run per arm, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, `trtllm-eval` with the same sparse-attention config as the decode-step runs:**

| Arm | GSM8K (%) |
|---|---|
| stock | 95.45 +- 0.57 |
| closed-loop | 95.53 +- 0.57 |
| prescore | 95.00 +- 0.60 |

All arms are within one standard error (~0.6) and inside the recorded reference band for this checkpoint (95.11-95.38). GSM8K prompts are shorter than the emission floor (2048 compressed positions), so both emission arms run the stock Top-K on these samples; the run-to-run spread is the baseline's own non-determinism. Exactness of the prescore tier itself is covered by the deterministic long-context cells above (136/136 identical tokens at 256k and 1M).

### Tests

- `test_cute_dsl_gvr_topk_decode.py`: 362 passed, 1 xpassed; adds the routing-floor test and a 90-cell direct single-band consumer test (K 512/1024/2048 x N 16k/64k/256k x five list shapes x randn/relu, one fallback row per cell: exact top-K, prior mirror, neighbour flags, histogram reset).
- `test_cute_dsl_gvr_topk_tiers.py`: 95 passed, 8 skipped.
- `test_cute_dsl_fp4_paged_mqa_logits.py -k "block_meta or seed_counts or cand or derive_lines"`: 280 passed under `-n 8` (the `_cand` test now compares logits inside `[0, ctx)` only: the runner returns an arena slice whose columns past the row are undefined, and the earlier xdist-only mismatches were recycled NaN in that tail) (`derive_lines`: lines bitwise equal to the torch reference, identical single-band list vs. seed-row lines, sub-K samples -> +inf, histogram untouched; `cand_single_band`: exact n0, A/B untouched, C == {>= t0}). `test_cute_dsl_fp8_paged_mqa_logits.py`: 176 passed, file identical to main.
- `test_dsa_indexer.py -k "gvr_prescore or use_gvr"`: 11 passed (chained FP4 decode over cr 1/4 x batch 2/8/16: sound line, single-band admission, prior mirroring, histogram reset every step, value-exact Top-K; config-field threading and default-off).

## Scope and follow-up

Off by default: on DeepSeek-V4-Flash the prescore chain is 1.3-1.6x the stock V1 chain at 64k-256k (0.83x at 1M) and 1.6-2.0x the hint-free V2 chain at kernel level, so there is no speed case for enabling it; the remaining cost is the prescore kernel's dependency-chain floor (~7.4 us per layer) and the scorer's emission epilogue (+2.5 to +5.5 us per layer). Its value is a fallback-free, predictable list path. The list consumer keeps the existing rank-scatter selection: an anchored-radix rewrite in the self-sampling style (256-bin histogram, count crossing, parked-class refinement) measured 1.0-1.8 us per layer slower on real rows and was not adopted. Not in this PR: FP8 (DeepSeek-V3.2) prescore wiring (paired measurement loses 1.02-1.84x there), MTP rows (the tier is gated to next_n == 1), a deeper prescore/scorer fusion (deferred emission so the scorer can start with the prescore; modelled 64k span ~15.7 us, still above V2's 11.9), DeepSeek-V4-Pro and MTP3 end-to-end cells.

items.title: [https://nvbugs/6732123][fix] Correct V2 KV cache quota estimation
items.body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

Fix three V2 KV cache sizing failures in one PR: PARD's separate draft pool can be too small to allocate or resume, GPT-OSS with finite window overrides can report hundreds of GiB of mandatory fixed cache, and layer-wise hybrid benchmarks can underallocate attention pages for their synthetic requests.

- Share context, generation-headroom, and SWA boundary-page accounting between static estimation and runtime quota conversion. Preserve the external drafter's fixed pool and page-rounded resume capacity. Estimate the standalone draft cost directly when splitting target/draft budgets.
- Keep the existing `CacheCost(slope, intercept)` model. Explicit native `full_attention` layers contribute to the slope even when a runtime window override bounds retention; native SWA and external draft pools retain fixed costs. Runtime windows are unchanged. No separate budget-estimation mode or `for_budget_split` parameter is needed. Configured target/draft quotas still sum to the input budget.
- Set `avg_seq_len=max_seq_len` in the layer-wise benchmark, where every dummy request actually has that length. Keep this workload correction in the benchmark rather than changing the hybrid pool solver.

PARD/DFlash allocation and resume regressions run in the GPU unit-test lane. The focused Nemotron/Qwen3-Next benchmark cases select V2 directly, without adding duplicate V1 CI cases. This PR incorporates the fixes from #18932 and #18954.

The native-full classification relies on explicit layer metadata; configs without it retain existing behavior. This is a static affine estimate, not an exact saturation curve for arbitrary all-SWA workloads.

The SWA context and boundary-page reservations also apply to ordinary target models with speculative decoding disabled. For a Gemma3-27B-shaped configuration (30 SWA layers at window 1024, 10 full-attention layers, 2048 bytes/token/layer, 64-token blocks, batch size 8, and `max_num_tokens=8192`), the fixed cost with scratch reuse disabled increases from 480 MiB (~0.47 GiB) to 990 MiB (~0.97 GiB): 480 MiB for context capacity and 30 MiB for retained boundary pages. Lower estimated token capacity under the same GPU memory budget is an expected consequence of correcting the earlier underestimation. Static estimation reads scratch reuse from `KvCacheConfig` and keeps it disabled for draft managers, matching runtime.

## Test Coverage

- Merged main at `e13e487195`; the related suite passed again on the merged revision: **142 passed**. Main removed the Llama-3.1-8B accuracy suite in #18809, including the old PARD overlap cases; this PR preserves that removal and retains the CUDA-backed PARD/DFlash quota regressions.
- CI lane correction: moved both CUDA-backed external-draft regressions out of the module-level `cpu_only` estimator file into `test_kv_cache_manager_v2.py`. Existing H100/B300/GB300 executor entries cover that file with `-m "not cpu_only"`; adding a GPU marker alone would not cancel an inherited CPU marker. Validated the CI marker expressions on B200: **40 passed, 54 deselected** with CUDA hidden and `-m cpu_only`; **54 passed, 3 deselected** with `-m "not cpu_only"`, including both PARD and DFlash regressions with no skips.
- Final combined budget split, cache estimation, V2 manager, and focused hybrid/MTP suite on B200: **142 passed**, including GPU allocation tests.

items.title: [None][fix] Size the FlashInfer page-index buffer for VSWA on V1 KV cache
items.body:
## Description

`FlashInferAttentionMetadata._post_init_with_buffers` read
`kv_cache_manager.blocks_in_primary_pool` directly to seed `max_num_blocks`,
which sizes the flat `_paged_kv_indices` buffer and the per-pool VSWA buffers.
That scalar is not part of the KV cache manager interface:

* `KVCacheManagerV2` always exposes it as a property.
* The V1 `KVCacheManager` only assigns it when it ends up with a single pool.
  The VSWA sizing path (`calculate_max_num_blocks_for_vswa()`) fills the
  `blocks_per_window` dict instead and leaves the scalar unset, as the standing
  `FIXME` next to it in `pyexecutor/resource_manager.py` already notes ("only
  covers the single window case and not VSWA scheme").

Any VSWA model routed to a V1 manager therefore dies in metadata construction
with:

```
AttributeError: 'KVCacheManager' object has no attribute 'blocks_in_primary_pool'
```

Disaggregated serving is one such route: `llm_utils.py` keeps a model's V2
preference only for the NIXL + Python-transceiver combination and otherwise
falls back to V1, so a VSWA model that runs fine aggregated crashes as soon as a
cache transceiver is configured.

The fix routes the read through a small `_get_blocks_in_primary_pool()` helper:

* use `blocks_in_primary_pool` when the manager exposes it (V2, single-pool V1);
* otherwise take the largest primary count from `blocks_per_window`. That is an
  upper bound across the pools, so the buffer stays large enough for every
  pool, and it feeds the same `max_num_blocks` seed that the per-layer buffer
  sizes are folded into;
* raise a named `AttributeError` describing both missing attributes when
  neither is available, instead of an anonymous attribute read.

This matches the `getattr`-guarded V2-only lookups a few lines further down in
the same function ("V1 managers lack the per-pool infrastructure"). The
`FIXME` in `resource_manager.py` is left in place; its other point
(single-window-only semantics of the scalar) still stands.

## Test Coverage

Unit test (CPU-only, stub managers):

`tests/unittest/_torch/attention/test_flashinfer_attention.py::TestFlashInferAttention::test_blocks_in_primary_pool_falls_back_to_blocks_per_window`

* a V2-shaped manager returns the scalar even when a `blocks_per_window` table
  is also present;
* a V1 VSWA-shaped manager (no scalar, three windows) returns the largest
  per-window primary count;
* a manager with neither attribute, or an empty `blocks_per_window`, raises an
  `AttributeError` that names the manager type and the missing attributes.

The failure this fixes was first hit in disaggregated serving of a VSWA model
whose class prefers the V2 KV cache manager but was demoted to V1: engine setup
aborted during metadata construction with the `AttributeError` above. This
change removes that crash by sizing the buffer from the per-window table when
the scalar is absent; the guard itself is covered by the unit test above.

items.title: [#18849][fix] Pass vocab_size to hybrid-Mamba KV cache managers
items.body:
## Description

Fixes https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/issues/18849.

`_create_kv_cache_manager` passed `vocab_size=config.vocab_size` on the MLA branch and the plain-attention branch only. The three hybrid-Mamba branches (Kimi K3 / KDA, `nemotron_hybrid`, and `qwen3_next` / Qwen3.5 / Qwen4-Exp) constructed the manager without it, and `MambaHybridCacheManagerV2` absorbs unknown keywords through `**kwargs`, so `KVCacheManagerV2.vocab_size` silently stayed `None`.

That field is read only when building multimodal block-reuse cache keys (`_augment_tokens_with_mm_run_metadata` / `_augment_tokens_with_contiguous_mm_metadata`), which is why a hybrid deployment serves text-only traffic indefinitely and then dies on its first `image_url` request: `gen_multimodal_cache_key_tokens()` receives `None` as `id_offset`, the resulting `TypeError` escapes into the PyExecutor event loop, and every rank is hard-killed.

Two changes:

1. `vocab_size` moves into `manager_extra_kwargs`, which is already gated on `issubclass(kv_cache_manager_cls, KVCacheManagerV2)`, and the two per-branch `vocab_size=config.vocab_size` arguments are removed. Every V2 branch now gets the value from one place, so a branch added later cannot omit it — the same reasoning `_mamba_conv_layout_kwargs` already applies to `conv_state_layout`. The V1 managers are unaffected: `KVCacheManager` swallowed the argument into `**kwargs` without reading it, and `MixedMambaHybridCacheManager` (which has no `**kwargs`) must not receive it.
2. The new `_resolve_vocab_size` helper falls back to `text_config.vocab_size`, because composite VLM configs keep the field on the nested text config.

Additionally, `KVCacheManagerV2._augment_tokens_for_block_reuse` now raises a `RuntimeError` naming the missing construction argument when it is asked to build multimodal cache keys without a `vocab_size`, rather than letting `None` reach the binding. Text-only requests return before that check, so they are unaffected.

Not addressed here, to keep this PR to one concern: suggestion 3 in the issue — failing the individual request with a 4xx instead of terminating the executor when multimodal metadata cannot be built (which also covers the `disable_mm_encoder: true` case). That is executor-level error classification and is worth its own PR, so it is now tracked separately in #18971.

I do not have Hopper hardware, so the end-to-end reproduction from the issue was not re-run; the reporter's verified workaround fills in the same value this change now passes.

## Test Coverage

`tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_mamba_cache_manager.py`
- `test_hybrid_v2_manager_receives_vocab_size` — routes a Qwen3 hybrid config through `_create_kv_cache_manager` and asserts the V2 manager is constructed with `vocab_size`. Fails on `main`.
- `test_hybrid_v2_manager_reads_vocab_size_from_text_config` — same, with `vocab_size` only on the nested `text_config`.
- `test_hybrid_v1_manager_does_not_receive_vocab_size` — guards the V1 `MixedMambaHybridCacheManager`, whose signature has no `**kwargs`.

- `test_augment_tokens_for_block_reuse_reports_missing_vocab_size` — the guard names the missing argument.
- `test_augment_tokens_for_block_reuse_ignores_missing_vocab_size_for_text` — text-only requests still work without a `vocab_size`.

Both files are CPU-only. `pre-commit`'s formatters and linters (ruff 0.9.4 check/format on the Group A files, yapf 0.43.0 / isort 5.12.0 / `ruff-legacy` on `_util.py`, codespell) pass on the changed files. items.title: [None][feat] Add calibrated INT8 KV cache to PyTorch backend
items.body:
## Summary

Add calibrated INT8 KV-cache storage to the PyTorch TRTLLM attention backend for dense decoder-only models with FP16/BF16 projections. `KvCacheConfig(dtype="int8")` reaches checkpoint loading, fused-QKV scale parameters, attention, and both KV-cache managers. This addresses the INT8 KV-cache item in #3701.

The unquantized fused-QKV weight path now has one cache-scale loading hook for INT8 and FP4. INT8 requires paired positive finite scalar `k_scale`/`v_scale` tensors, uses their maximum for the existing native shared K/V scale, and preserves scale pointers on reload. FP4 retains its optional per-K/V scale loading and environment opt-out; INT8 rejects `TRTLLM_LOAD_KV_SCALES=0` to prevent uncalibrated unity scales. Cache accounting, including V2 static fraction-based capacity estimation, uses one byte per INT8 element; allocator granularity still applies.

## Supported scope

Full prefill followed by single-token decode, paged cache storage, unquantized FP16/BF16 dense decoder projections, TRTLLM attention backend. Disable chunked prefill and prefix block reuse. Reject unsupported cached prefill, speculative decoding, MLA, sparse/cross attention, context parallelism, hybrid models, quantized projections, disaggregated serving, and KV connectors.

Decode-only calls skip the cached-context list scan. Tensor and cache-metadata guards remain per-call because a backend caller can replace its inputs after warmup; tests cover those replacements rather than caching the first validation result indefinitely.

## Shared FMHA prerequisite

Full prefill exposed a missing `cu_kv_seqlens` pointer in packed-QKV FMHA, also reproducible with FP16 cache. The pointer initialization remains a prerequisite in this PR. The new independent `test_packed_qkv_fmha.py` verifies FP16/BF16, MHA/GQA, and unequal context lengths against the Vanilla backend, and asserts the fallback packed-QKV path is actually selected without KV quantization.

These eight regression cases are registered explicitly for A10 and B200; H100 collects them through its existing `unittest/_torch/attention` directory entry. Stage mapping was checked. Only SM89 was executed on the remote RTX 4090; Hopper/Blackwell CI results are still required before merge. The native fix has not been split into another PR.

## Validation

On remote RTX 4090, PyTorch 2.12.0+cu130 and CUDA 13.0, at `e2a0a813cf53cbd7df8f83cb0754fd56d542df93`:

- 96 tests passed: 20 config/accounting, 20 scale-loading/compatibility, 46 INT8 attention, two full checkpoint/LLM tests, and eight independent full-precision FMHA cases.
- 81 existing cache estimation/budget regression tests passed.
- All 54 attention tests passed Compute Sanitizer with zero memory errors (`--report-api-errors no` suppresses import-time CUDA API probes).
- With CUDA devices hidden: 20 CPU tests passed, 76 CUDA-dependent tests skipped.
- New sizing/transfer-guard tests reproduced four failures on the previous implementation before the fixes.
- Full checkpoint tests use explicitly resolved INT8 with V1 and V2, exercise fraction-based capacity estimation, and compare eager versus CUDA Graph generation using the same cache dtype. They no longer require token equality between FP16 and INT8 caches.
- Full pre-commit and DCO commit hooks passed. Test-list AST validation and A10/H100/B200 stage mapping were checked.

Python changes use the previously rebuilt native libraries from this PR. That build compiled 101 affected objects, updated three static archives, and relinked the core library, Torch library and bindings. Unchanged objects/dependencies were reused from an existing rc26 build; it was not a clean full build. This update does not change native code. Multi-GPU and other GPU architectures have not been exercised by this validation.

## Quantization quality limitation

The native path uses a single shared scalar for K and V. The earlier Qwen2.5-0.5B calibration experiment exposed a roughly 603x K/V range mismatch in the first layer and degraded generated text with the shared scale. Additional checkpoint balancing was diagnostic only and is not shipped in this change. This review update does not establish model-quality acceptance or serving speedup. Checkpoint scales must be calibrated for INT8, including rotary K ranges, and model quality requires representative evaluation.

items.body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

Cache Manager V2 now accounts for standalone draft managers and PARD runtime headroom. Budget splitting preserves separate target and draft affine costs, including SWA, retained pages, rounding, and resume costs. Shared headroom logic applies to estimation, quota conversion, allocation growth, and `max_blocks_per_seq`. The generic `CacheCost` model remains unchanged. Main regression risk is inconsistency between static sizing and runtime allocation for uncommon speculative-decoding configurations.

## QA Engineer Review

Four KV-cache unit-test files and one integration test file changed. Coverage includes PARD headroom, affine budget splitting, SWA and rounding costs, draft-cache reuse, resume behavior, quota expectations, and maximum block capacity. The reported 329 KV-cache V2 tests pass. `test_pard` is listed in both the QA list and the `l0_h100` CI list. Coverage verdict: **sufficient**.

### Per-File QA Perspective

- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/_util.py`: Verify target and draft cost estimation with standalone and one-model draft layouts, configured token limits, SWA fixed costs, and GPU-budget error reporting.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/kv_cache/kv_cache_manager_v2.py`: Verify consistent speculative headroom across static estimation, runtime growth, draft reservations, block limits, SWA, rounding, and resume behavior.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_kv_cache_budget_split.py`: Covers explicit draft intercepts, slot inflation, boundary/context blocks, and fixed-cost allocation. This unit test is not an integration test-list entry.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_kv_cache_estimation.py`: Covers sliding-window allocation, speculative decoding, draft reuse, PARD/DFLASH cost derivation, resume utilization, and generation headroom. This unit test is not an integration test-list entry.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_kv_cache_manager_v2.py`: Covers PARD manager capacity, generation headroom, and ledger-block rounding across cache tiers. This unit test is not an integration test-list entry.
- `tests/integration/defs/accuracy/test_llm_api_pytorch.py`: Updates `test_pard` to use V2 KV cache management, block reuse, and an 80% free-memory fraction. The test is listed in `tests/integration/test_lists/qa/llm_function_core.txt` and `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_h100.yml`.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

Cache manager V2 could under-size the standalone draft KV pool used by one-engine external drafters such as PARD. A logical PARD draft length of K consumes 2K runtime tokens per generation step; for K=4, the maximum KV capacity lead is `(K - 1) + 2K = 11` tokens.

This change keeps KV cost accounting purely affine (`slope * tokens + intercept`) while making the estimator match runtime allocation geometry:

- estimate the standalone draft manager directly and preserve its independent slope/intercept when splitting target and draft budgets;
- use the same speculative-generation headroom for estimation, quota conversion, allocation growth, and `max_blocks_per_seq`;
- include fixed SWA context/generation capacity, retained boundary pages, page-granularity rounding, and the resume watermark in the manager-owned intercept.

The generic `CacheCost` model is unchanged; manager-specific pool geometry remains encapsulated in the V2 estimator.

The one-model target/draft joint-reuse fix now present on `main` is also required for correct PARD block-reuse behavior and acceptance length. The PARD integration results below validate the combined behavior after rebasing onto that fix; they do not attribute the acceptance-length improvement to this accounting change alone.

## Test Coverage

items.title: [None][chore] Assert KV cache liveness on the V2 disagg transfer path
items.body:
## Description

This is non-functional change. Only adding assertion for code completeness.

V2's disaggregated KV transfer builds peer pointers as `base + stride * slot_id` from
`get_aggregated_page_indices`, which carries no cache level. The arithmetic is only valid while
the request's KV cache is ACTIVE, so its pages are GPU-locked. That precondition was stated in a
comment; V1 asserts the equivalent in C++.

This makes it explicit:

- `_CacheReuseAdapterV2.get_block_ids` asserts the cache is active before returning slot ids.
- The V2 scheduler skips requests whose KV may still be read or written by the fabric when
  choosing an eviction or recompute-pause victim, using the existing
  `_is_request_in_transmission` predicate instead of relying on request-state numbering.

## Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_kv_cache_v2_scheduler.py::TestInTransmissionVictims`
  — a request in transmission is not chosen as an eviction victim under KV pressure, and is not
  recompute-paused; paired controls show the same request *is* taken when it is not in
  transmission.
- `tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_cache_reuse_adapter.py::TestPackedBeamBlockLayout::test_v2_adapter_returns_slot_ids_for_an_active_cache`
  and `::test_v2_adapter_rejects_a_suspended_cache` — the adapter's precondition, both ways.

items.title: [None][feat] Merge back locality domain support for KV cache and two-stream attention
items.body:
> Merge-back from the internal Rubin feature branch, sliced by path. This slice is the
> KV cache runtime layer plus the locality-domain two-stream attention path.

## Description

A locality domain splits a GPU into halves with their own memory. This adds:

- **KV cache runtime** — slot allocation, free-slot preparation, page indexing
  and eviction take a `locality_domain_id`; GPU storage backs each domain with its own
  physical memory. Existing callers move to keyword arguments so the new parameter
  cannot bind positionally.
- **Two-stream attention** (`attention/backends/trtllm.py`) — each domain runs on its
  own stream; per-domain metadata,
  workspaces, block offsets and KV lengths; the batch is sorted by domain so each
  domain's slice is contiguous.
- **Model engine / py_executor** — requests are assigned a domain and reordered by it;
  `attn_metadata` carries the per-domain request/token split points; CUDA graph warmup
  gives each active domain one max-length dummy request.
- **`thop/cublasScaledMM.cpp`** — the cuBLAS wrapper is keyed by `CUcontext`, since each
  domain runs under its own green context.

Locality domains are Python-backend only. On the C++ backend
`enable_locality_domains=True` raises `NotImplementedError` rather than silently
returning a non-localized cache.

Also fixes `pool_group_descs`, which called `num_slots()` without a domain id and made
locality-domain startup fail outright. `base_address` is slot 0's address, which lives
in domain 0, so the slot count now describes the same domain.

**Not included:** `modules/linear.py` and `models/modeling_deepseekv3.py` (MLA). Those
are a separate internal MR, so locality domains are not exercisable on MLA models yet.

## Test Coverage

`tests/unittest/kv_cache_manager_v2_tests/` — allocation, resize, suspend/resume,
eviction filtering, salted reuse, page indexing, non-localized backward compatibility.
`tests/integration/defs/kv_cache/test_stream_localization_e2e.py` — localized vs
baseline output equivalence.
`tests/unittest/_torch/executor/test_pytorch_model_engine.py` — CUDA graph warmup
request split.

Verified on GB200 with mock localization (`num_domains=2`, `fork_join=True`): greedy
output byte-identical to the non-localized baseline. Green contexts and real VMM
behaviour need Rubin and are not covered here.

## PR Checklist

- [x] PR title follows the format
- [x] Tests added/updated
- [x] Documentation not required

- Verifies `~/` expansion, unset-`HOME` handling, and managed-workspace behavior.
- No integration test-list files changed. Registration is not applicable to these unit tests.
- Coverage verdict: **sufficient**.

## Per-File QA Perspective

- `docs/source/llm-api/index.md`: Verify documented cache precedence, worker propagation, DeepGEMM persistence, and FlashInfer isolation.
- `tensorrt_llm/__init__.py`: Verify bootstrap comments match environment initialization order.
- `tensorrt_llm/_bootstrap.py`: Verify unified cache defaults apply only when variables are unset and configure DeepGEMM correctly.
- `tensorrt_llm/executor/ray/gpu_worker.py`: Verify explicit `DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR` values remain unchanged and fallback paths remain rank- and GPU-specific.
- `tensorrt_llm/llmapi/mpi_session.py`: Verify approved cache variables reach MPI workers without changing existing environment forwarding.
- `tensorrt_llm/llmapi/trtllm-llmapi-launch`: Verify workspace expansion, explicit workspace precedence, trailing-slash handling, standalone `~` handling, and the unset-`HOME` fallback.
- `tests/unittest/llmapi/test_mpi_session.py`: Covers launcher expansion and managed-workspace behavior. No integration test-list entry changed.
- `tests/unittest/test_unified_cache.py`: Covers unified-cache setup, overrides, initialization ordering, MPI propagation, DeepGEMM settings, and FlashInfer isolation. No integration test-list entry changed.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

TRT-LLM currently uses a large variety of caches (e.g., Flashinfer, DeepGEMM, auto-tuner) that can all be configured via separate environment variables, which is cumbersome for end users. At the same time, leveraging warmed-up caches is a good way to speed up TRT-LLM startup and avoid re-compilation of JIT artifacts.

This PR simplifies the above by introducing a `TRTLLM_CACHE_DIR` environment variable which, when set, sets a single root cache directory, under which all known framework caches will be contained. At the moment `TRTLLM_CACHE_DIR` controls the following:

- `TLLM_AUTOTUNER_CACHE_PATH`
- `TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR`
- `TRITON_CACHE_DIR`
- `TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR`
- `FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE`
- `CUTE_DSL_CACHE_DIR`
- `DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR`
- `TRTLLM_DG_CACHE_DIR`
- `CUDA_CACHE_PATH`

If any of these variables is explicitly set alongside `TRTLLM_CACHE_DIR`, then the framework-specific environment variables will take precedence. Also note that the `TRTLLM_DG_JIT_DUMP_CUBIN` environment variable will be set automatically together with `TRTLLM_CACHE_DIR`, in order to enable cubin dumping in DeepGEMM at `TRTLLM_DG_CACHE_DIR`. Additional caches could be added in the future using the same mechanism.

The unified caching implementation does not collide with the per-rank cache isolation mechanism implemented for Flashinfer: generally, isolation will be enabled if neither of `TRTLLM_CACHE_DIR` or `FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE` are set.

## Test Coverage

A series of focused tests was added to ensure that cache priorities are respected (e.g., individual framework caches over `TRTLLM_CACHE_DIR`), that Flashinfer isolation works as expected, and that the proper environment variables are passed from the main process to the MPI workers.

items.title: [None][perf] reuse emptied host KV cache slots before eviction
items.body:
## Problem this solves

When a KV-cache block is onboarded from secondary storage, `WindowBlockManager::onboardBlock` copies its content into a fresh primary block and swaps the two blocks' memory-pool offsets. The original secondary slot is therefore left empty.

Today that empty slot is returned at the default retention priority and appended to the back of the secondary LRU queue. `LRUEvictionPolicy::getFreeBlock(kSecondaryLevel)` selects the front of the lowest non-empty priority queue, so the allocator can evict every reusable host block ahead of the empty slot before it reaches the slot that contains no data at all. Each onboard can effectively remove one host slot from useful capacity for an entire LRU rotation.

This shows up in long-context, multi-turn agent workloads that repeatedly onboard old prefixes while concurrently offloading newer prefixes. Despite having empty secondary slots, the cache can evict live host content and later recompute those long-gap prefixes.

## What changes

After the onboard swap, this PR returns the emptied secondary slot at minimum retention priority and at the front of its free queue:

```cpp
block->setPriority(executor::KvCacheRetentionConfig::kMinRetentionPriority);
mEvictionPolicy->releaseBlock(block, /*toFront=*/true);
```

The next offload therefore fills the empty slot before evicting host content that is still eligible for reuse. This is the same reclaim-first principle already used when detached blocks are returned to the eviction policy.

The production behavior is two statements. The surrounding comment documents why both the priority and queue position matter.

This change is deliberately isolated to the empty-slot lifecycle. It does not include prefix-walk, scheduler, quantization, kernel, or configuration changes.

## Why this is safe

At this point in `onboardBlock`, `block` is the fresh primary block returned by `getFreeBlock`, after its memory-pool offset has been swapped with the onboarded block:

- it contains no reusable KV-cache content;
- it has no references;
- it is detached from the reuse lookup tree;
- `getFreeBlock` has already cleared any duration associated with its prior use.

Minimum retention priority correctly describes an empty slot: there is no content to retain. When the slot is selected for a later offload, `claimBlock` resets its retention metadata before new content is installed. Consequently, the slot does not acquire stale expiration behavior.

The transfer and synchronization sequence is unchanged. The copy completes through the existing transfer manager, offsets are swapped at the same point, and the slot is released only afterward. `WindowBlockManager::offloadBlock` continues to return the emptied primary slot through its existing path.

KV-cache events also become more accurate: the onboard and subsequent offload still emit their cache-level update events, but there is no removal event for a reusable host block because no reusable host block was evicted.

## Tests

The new regression test constructs four primary and four secondary blocks, then:

1. allocates a three-block sequence;
2. offloads its first block and records the secondary memory-pool slot;
3. onboards that block, leaving the recorded secondary slot empty;
4. offloads a second live block;
5. verifies that the second block lands in the recorded empty slot;
6. verifies queue integrity and that the offloaded block retains its own normal priority.

Without this fix, step 5 fails because the allocator selects an unused slot farther back in the default-priority queue. With the fix, it selects the just-emptied minimum-priority slot first.

The existing KV-cache event-stream test is also updated to expect one onboard and one offload event with no removal event for this sequence.

Validation performed:

- `BlockManagerOnboardReleasesEmptiedHostSlotFirst` passed on a CUDA-enabled build of the same change.
- Filtered `kvCacheManagerTest` suite: 189/189 passed on that CUDA-enabled build.
- `pre-commit run clang-format --files cpp/tensorrt_llm/batch_manager/kvCacheManager.cpp cpp/tests/unit_tests/batch_manager/kvCacheManagerTest.cpp` passed on this `main` port.
- `git diff --check` passed.

The CUDA suite has not been rerun locally on this exact `main` commit because the development host used for the port has no NVIDIA GPU. CI should rerun the C++ unit suite against current `main`.

## Cache-retention and performance evidence

The issue was found with DRAM KV offload under a long-context, multi-turn agent trace whose returning prompts frequently reuse hundreds of thousands of tokens. Runtime/replay analysis showed that approximately 45-51% of secondary slots could be empty on average while long-idle continuations still lost reusable host prefixes. That combination is inconsistent with a capacity-only explanation and matches the queue-rotation mechanism above.

In an isolated same-node A/B at fixed offered work, changing only the empty-slot reclaim behavior produced:

| Metric | Existing behavior | Reclaim empty slot first | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Long-gap achieved/offered prefix reuse | 97.58% | 99.93% | +2.35 percentage points |
| Effective input throughput per GPU | baseline | 1.0093x baseline | +0.93% |
| Short-gap prefix reuse | unchanged | unchanged | no regression |

The throughput cell was client-paced and already close to its maximum attainable reuse, so the direct throughput delta is intentionally reported as a bounded result, not a universal expectation. The larger practical benefit is avoiding a cache/TTFT cliff as each prefill worker carries more concurrent long-context sessions: reclaiming empty slots preserves useful host residency and lets the configured host tier behave closer to its nominal capacity.

Profiling found no material change in GPU kernel families, as expected for an eviction-order fix. The improvement appeared in the host resource-preparation path: previously exposed onboard/admission work was substantially reduced after long-gap prefix retention recovered.


### Replay and full-workload context

A block-level retention replay driven by the measured request reuse-distance distribution and host-pool geometry reproduced the stock long-gap loss. With reclaim-first ordering, it projected long-gap achieved/offered prefix reuse of **97.9% at 6 prefill workers** and **94.9% at 5 prefill workers**. This is mechanism and capacity-pressure evidence, not a standalone throughput benchmark.

The host-slot-only A/B above deliberately measures this PR in isolation. Two additional full, concurrency-227 GLM-5.2 AgentX measurements tested whether the corrected host path survived sustained load. They held scheduler configuration and topology fixed while moving from the configuration-only executable to an executable containing both this change and the linear prefix-reuse walk from [#17848](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/17848):

| Disaggregated topology | TPS/GPU, before | TPS/GPU, combined code | Change | Total backend TPS | p90 TPS/user | TTFT p90 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 6P + 1D, decode EP8 | 33,668.13 | 36,717.90 | **+9.06%** | 1,077,380 to 1,174,973 | 84.995 to 84.747 | not isolated |
| 5P + 1D, decode EP8 | 35,237.05 | 41,522.73 | **+17.84%** | 986,637 to 1,162,636 | 80.923 to 85.286 | 12.34 s to 3.30 s |

These full-load deltas are **combined-stack evidence**, not standalone attribution to this PR: they include #17848 and interaction between faster admission, retained host capacity, and load per prefill worker. A smaller proxy isolated #17848 at +3.54% on top of the same scheduler setting, but that number must not simply be subtracted from the table because the two fixes interact. The defensible isolated attribution for this PR remains the host-slot-only result above: +2.35 percentage points of long-gap reuse and +0.93% effective input TPS/GPU in the already client-paced cell.

Matched Nsight profiles support the host-side mechanism. No material GPU kernel-family change appeared. Instead, exposed `prepare_resources` time fell from **4.9 ms to 0.2 ms**, while `_prepare_inputs` p90 fell from approximately **81-170 ms to 26-37 ms** across the observed windows as repeated host onboarding/admission stalls disappeared.

## Relationship to existing eviction work and duplicate audit

This change extends the reclaim-first rule already merged in [#11685](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/11685). That PR sends detached blocks released at request completion to the front of the free queue. It does not cover `onboardBlock`: after the memory-pool offset swap, this path directly calls `releaseBlock(block)` without the detached-block ordering used by `releaseBlocks`. The empty secondary slot can therefore remain behind live reusable host blocks despite #11685.

Current `main` at `ba32790910d126c72ad426e1ddc88c15974adf01` still contains that default-priority, back-of-queue release. Commit history and blame show no later change to this onboard lifecycle.

All ten other open PRs that touch `kvCacheManager.cpp` or its header were also inspected for an equivalent fix. None changes this host-tier release behavior. The closest overlap is [#16252](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/16252), which gives newly introduced disk-tier empty slots minimum priority, but its existing host-tier `onboardBlock` branch still uses the unchanged `releaseBlock(block)` call. Other open work touching onboarding, transfer preparation, radix-tree eviction, or cache events likewise leaves this lifecycle gap open.

## Functional and performance impact

- **Correctness:** no KV contents, offsets, copy ordering, or reference ownership changes.
- **Eviction policy:** only empty secondary slots are moved ahead of retained secondary content.
- **Events:** a later offload no longer reports removal of live host content when an empty slot is available.
- **Performance:** neutral when the secondary tier is unused or has no reuse pressure; positive when onboard/offload churn would otherwise strand empty slots behind retained blocks.
- **Memory:** no allocation-size or capacity change.

## Diff size

Against current `main`:

| Scope | Insertions | Deletions |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Production | 11 | 2 |
| Tests | 85 | 5 |
| Total | 96 | 7 |

Only two production statements change behavior; the remaining production additions explain the queue and retention rules.

## Limitations

- The measured A/B used DRAM secondary storage. The lifecycle correction is common to other local secondary transfer modes, but they were not separately benchmarked.
- The gain depends on workload reuse distance and host-tier pressure. Workloads without onboarding or with a cold/unused host tier should not be expected to improve.
- This PR does not alter host-cache sizing or admission policy; it makes existing secondary capacity reusable in the correct order.

items.title: [None][fix] Emit multimodal keys in KV cache v2 events

labels.name: api-compatible
labels.description: Accepted LLM API contract change that is backwards-compatible

items.body:
## Description

KV cache manager v2 stored events currently omit multimodal keys. Generate `mm_keys` directly from the actual cached block's native digest and continuation tokens in both the C++ and Python event managers. Each key contains the item digest and item-local start offset, including items spanning blocks and runs separated by text.

Radix blocks retain the latest prefix digest when MM event decoding is enabled, so event generation reads the direct parent's context without walking the ancestor chain. The immutable digest remains valid across detach/reattach and does not retain ancestor blocks or pages. Complete MM keys belong to the event payload. Forward the vocabulary offset through ordinary and hybrid V2 manager construction.

V2 emits the item digest as a hexadecimal string. Optional UUIDs continue to participate in upstream item hashing with the content; V1 still exposes an original UUID when supplied. Token encoding and block hashing are unchanged. The block context adds a shared-pointer field even when events are disabled; digest-context maintenance is enabled only when needed for events.

## Test Coverage

- Native B200 build passed with `--cuda_architectures=100-real`.
- CPU wrapper/factory and Python detached-ancestor regressions: **21 passed**.
- Complete event-manager, stats, and salting modules: **93 passed** on the C++ backend; **83 passed, 10 expected native-only skips** on the Python backend.
- Coverage includes cross-block offsets, text-only/unpublished ancestors, lifecycle removal and republication, actual-node partial-prefix reuse, direct digest ownership, and ordinary/hybrid incremental commits.
- Pre-commit hooks passed, including clang-format, Python formatting/lint, codespell, DCO, and test-list validation. The review follow-up only reorders independent test assertions to avoid a merge conflict with main.

- Model-weight multimodal/E-P-D end-to-end tests and performance benchmarks were **not run**.
